id: title:DanielVisca:filter the change feed by kind

observations.behavior: Adds a new optional query parameter 'kinds' with an enum-like choice field for filtering the types of recorded events.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows users or automated agents (like MCP clients) to request specific subsets of historical data rather than all available event types.

observations.behavior: Implements backend filtering: it checks the incoming request and only includes visibility rules matching the requested kinds in the returned feed.
observations.posthog_connection: This is not just documentation; this is actual execution logic that filters results before returning them, reducing payload size and relevance noise.

observations.behavior: Defines Zod schema validation and default behavior for the client-side API parameters used by generated TypeScript tools.
observations.posthog_connection: Establishes type safety and defaults for external tool invocations, supporting consistent behavior across different entry points into PostHog's change-feed functionality.

observations.limitations: The implementation relies on existing helper fields and does not introduce complex business-logic changes. Tests are added but do not cover edge cases beyond basic rejection and kind-filtering assertions.

review.limitations: The implementation relies on existing helper fields and does not introduce complex business-logic changes. Tests are added but do not cover edge cases beyond basic rejection and kind-filtering assertions.
review.reason: A substantive, bounded capability improvement: adding a filterable dimension ('kinds') with both backend enforcement and frontend support. This could help reduce irrelevant entries when users or automated agents investigate configuration-only changes without releases or annotations.
review.posthog_relevance: Adds value to warehouse ingestion workflows and debugging scenarios where distinguishing between release events versus annotation/flag edits matters. It also supports MCP clients and other programmatic accessors.
review.uncertainty: Assessment assumes no hidden dependencies; actual benefit depends on adoption of this filtering option rather than its mere presence.
